misconception.text: The pressure at depth $h$ in a fluid is $\rho g h$ below atmospheric pressure.

correction.text: The gauge pressure at depth $h$ is $\rho gh$, and the absolute pressure is that plus atmospheric. The pressure rises with depth, so a deeper point is at a higher pressure, not a lower one.

signal.text: Our own question offers the pressure below atmospheric as an option.

misconception.text: Gauge pressure is the total pressure in the fluid.

correction.text: Gauge pressure is the pressure in excess of atmospheric, so a gauge reading of zero means the pressure is atmospheric. The absolute pressure is the gauge pressure plus atmospheric.

signal.text: Our own question offers the total pressure as an option.
